tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: Open an intact inner blade–sheath junction: Echinochloa has no projecting membrane or ligule hair fringe (0 mm), and no auricles. The physically archived Harry Rose collar image is panel 2 and demonstrates this negative character; panel 3 shows the crowded branched head. A few nearby sheath hairs are not a ligule. E. muricata shares this character, so the collar alone does not settle introduced versus native identity.
tiles.short: A true ABSENT ligule, then a crowded branched panicle
tiles.status: COLLAR IMAGE PRESENT; TEXAS SAME-PLANT CALIBRATION NEEDED

tiles.heading: 02 · CHECK GROWTH & FLOWERING BRANCHES
tiles.details: Look for a fibrous-rooted annual, often 30–200 cm tall in Flora of North America, with a branched 5–25 cm terminal panicle and roughly 1.5–10 cm lateral branches. Physically archived Harry Rose panel 1 NOW shows a lifted tuft with multiple attached flowering heads, converging leafy culms and a partly obscured adhering root/soil mass, with three pixel-verified broad arrows. It is Australian, not a Texas voucher; it does not expose a cleaned complete root system. Panel 3 shows the crowded flowering branches; panel 7 is an external seedling reference.
tiles.status: ACTUAL CONNECTED LIFTED TUFT PHOTO — FULL ROOTS AND TEXAS VOUCHER MISSING

tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE ONE SPIKELET AND ITS GLUMES
tiles.details: At 10–20× isolate a mature spikelet about 2.5–4 mm long (excluding any awn), with a LOWER sterile and an UPPER fertile floret, not two separate spikelets. Lower glume is roughly 0.8–1.7 mm and usually 3–5-veined; upper glume is near full spikelet length, commonly 3–4 mm and 5-veined. Panel 5 is the photographer's annotated real spikelet and panel 6 shows two mature source-identified spikelets with three arrows to actual gross structures; neither is a measured Texas dissection proving glume venation or the diagnostic fertile-lemma apex.
tiles.short: 2.5–4 mm, two florets; lower glume shorter
tiles.status: REAL ANNOTATED + MATURE SPIKELET PHOTOS; CALIBRATED GLUMES STILL MISSING

tiles.heading: 04 · FIND THE ACTUAL LEMMA AWN
tiles.details: The lower sterile lemma is often approximately 3–4 mm and may be AWNLESS or carry a long terminal awn to about 50 mm, even varying along one panicle. The upper fertile lemma is about 2–3.5 mm with a hardened glossy body, and does NOT bear that long awn. Do not label a bristle on the flowering rachis as a lemma awn.
tiles.short: Lower sterile lemma awn 0–50 mm; fertile lemma hard
tiles.status: AWN VARIATION VISIBLE; INSERTION/MEASUREMENT PHOTO GAP

tiles.heading: 05 · NATIVE LOOK-ALIKE WARNING
tiles.details: Native rough barnyardgrass (E. muricata) can share the absent ligule, similar panicle and variable awns. For a confident E. crus-galli determination, dissect several ripe UPPER fertile lemmas at about 25–40×: the hard body ends abruptly at a thin withering tip separated by a transverse line of minute hairs. The current gallery does NOT independently resolve that line; otherwise record Echinochloa sp., not a native-versus-introduced verdict.
tiles.short: E. muricata ALSO has no ligule
tiles.status: CRITICAL NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — MATCHED MATURE LEMMA TIPS

tiles.heading: 06 · SPLIT OTHER LOCAL LOOK-ALIKES
tiles.details: Native E. muricata and introduced E. colona can also lack a ligule. Panicum capillare has a HAIR-FRINGE ligule and airy open panicle; Digitaria ciliaris has a MEMBRANOUS ligule and fingerlike racemes. Panel 8 is the DIFFERENT-SPECIES southern crabgrass seedhead, not a photographed crabgrass collar. Panel 2 is the actual Echinochloa absent-ligule photo; panel 3 shows the target head. For E. crus-galli versus E. muricata, dissect mature upper fertile lemma tips at 25–40× and inspect the minute transverse hairline; stop at Echinochloa sp. if unresolved.
tiles.short: Junglerice, witchgrass and crabgrass need collar checks
tiles.status: COMPARISON LESSON; PUBLIC PHOTO + SITE QA GAPS

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: BARNYARDGRASS: look first at a clean and intact grass BLADE–SHEATH junction: there is NO true ligule (neither projecting membrane nor fringe) and NO auricles. Our new licensed Harry Rose photo demonstrates this negative character, absent from older gallery. Next trace the crowded flowering panicle and its side branches; find mature true spikelets (typically 2.5–4 mm) with variable lower sterile-lemma awns. The new real author-labelled spikelet photograph teaches multiple florets as botanically distinct from separate spikelets. IMPORTANT: native E. muricata shares the absent ligule; never identify introduced E. crus-galli from a distant head alone. To distinguish it, examine the abruptly delimited thin terminal margin and short hair line on the mature upper fertile lemma at ~25–40x.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: START with PHYSICALLY ARCHIVED panel 1: the lifted Australian flowering tuft shows attached culms and branching heads with a partly obscured soil/root mass, NOT a fully cleaned root system or Texas voucher. Compare the archived panicle and crowded spikelets in panel 3.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Look for a fibrous-rooted annual, often 30–200 cm tall in Flora of North America, with a branched 5–25 cm terminal panicle and roughly 1.5–10 cm lateral branches. Physically archived Harry Rose panel 1 NOW shows a lifted tuft with multiple attached flowering heads, converging leafy culms and a partly obscured adhering root/soil mass, with three pixel-verified broad arrows. It is Australian, not a Texas voucher; it does not expose a cleaned complete root system. Panel 3 shows the crowded flowering branches; panel 7 is an external seedling reference.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: NO ligule helps distinguish Echinochloa from Digitaria ciliaris and Panicum capillare, but NOT E. crus-galli from E. muricata/colona/walteri. Species-level E. crus-galli is supported by a mature fertile lemma with abruptly delimited thin tip and tiny hairline; E. muricata lacks that demarcation. E. colona generally has smaller, less bristly short panicle branches; E. walteri has often hairy leaf sheaths. These alone are insufficient for assured species calls.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: WHOLE LIFTED ANNUAL TUFT — actual basal culms and attached flowering heads
panels.caption: Harry Rose's actual lifted Echinochloa crus-galli tuft from New South Wales. See how the erect culms and leaves converge to one grassy basal bunch, with an adhering dark root/soil clump at the lower edge. Multiple branched heads remain attached to the same tuft. This does NOT expose the complete fibrous root system, and is NOT a local Texas voucher.

panels.label: TRUE COLLAR — no ligule present · PROVISIONAL — USER PHOTO REVIEW PENDING
panels.caption: Harry Rose's image is of the true blade/split-sheath junction. The characteristic identification clue is what is MISSING: no projecting membranous ligule and no tuft constituting a ligule. Check several uninjured leaves; wear/damage may confuse a single collar. Pixel check (2026-10-23): the open green leaf sheath's top rim meets the upward blade here; there is no projecting membrane or fringe. This annotation targets the junction, not a purported tiny ligule.

memory_rule: NO LIGULE at true blade–sheath junction, broad sheaths/branched head, crowded awnless-or-awned spikelets. Barnyardgrass vs native rough barnyardgrass cannot be decided from absent ligule alone.
safety_note: Five genuine target-species JPEGs are now physically archived, including a true absent-ligule collar, two reproductive macro views and a connected lifted flowering tuft. The Australian source photos are not Texas vouchers and no image independently resolves the critical E. muricata fertile-lemma tip comparison.
field_rule: A species-name image from Commons is a taxon-labelled reference, not independent anatomical verification; use microscope for close E. crus-galli / E. muricata calls.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
